result:
The disk filled up and took the api with it. The `report-export` job started at 03:05:00 and wrote 40 CSV files of 512 MB each (about 20 GB) into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` over eight minutes, on the same volume the database uses. The disk warnings hit 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30, and at 03:14:00 the database failed:

`ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device`

The api aborted its transaction, shut down the worker pool and exited at 03:14:06 (`FATAL api: exiting (status 1)`). It never came back: the proxy logged `upstream api refused connection` every two minutes from 03:16:00 through 05:28:00 (67 times), and the log ends at 05:29:57 with no api restart. Dates in the log are 2026-03-09, so check this is the night you mean.

To recover, free space in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` and start the api again; nothing restarted it automatically. To prevent a repeat, the export needs to write to a different volume or clean up its parts. The job is not defined anywhere in this repo, so I could not see why it wrote so much.

The `cache: slow command` warnings (43, all 100–149 ms) run at a steady rate all night before and after the crash and look unrelated.
